To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified the genes that are involved in human airway repair.
we have identified a distinctive airway "repair transcriptome."
the airway epithelial transcriptome is altered after injury and that the alterations are consistent with the process of cell proliferation, redifferentiation, and repair.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new therapies for airway epithelial injury.
the molecular mechanisms underlying epithelial repair in the human lung.
the development and application of new technologies for the study of human airway epithelia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the repair process is a complex and dynamic process involving multiple gene products, including those involved in cell cycle, metabolism and transport and signal transduction.
the airway epithelial injury repair transcriptome at day 7 postinjury was dominated by cell-cycle, signal transduction and metabolism and transport genes.
this study provides a baseline of the genes that participate in the process of repair of the normal human airway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the human airway repair transcriptome is dominated by a proliferative, redifferentiation program, which is characterized by cell cycle, metabolism and transcription, signal transduction and transport gene expression.
the human airway transcriptome is altered in response to injury, with an early repair response that includes activation of genes involved in the cell cycle and cell proliferation.

the repair transcriptome at day 7 postinjury was dominated by cell proliferation, cell cycle, signal, transduction, metabolism, and transcription genes, whereas the expression profile was very similar to that of uninjured airway epithelum at day 14.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human airway repair transcriptome is a dynamic process with the majority of the changes occurring within 1 wk of injury.
there is a repair gene expression signature in the human airway that is distinct from the normal resting state.
the airway epithelial cells are capable of a robust response to injury and repair themselves.
